title: Why Do Astronauts Get Taller in Space?
short_title: Why Do Astronauts Get Taller in Space?
description_short:
Why do astronauts get taller in space? In microgravity, the spine is unloaded. It can straighten and lengthen, temporarily increasing an astronaut's height. NASA says the increase can reach about 3 percent. It's not bone growth, and it doesn't last: back on Earth, gravity loads the spine again and astronauts return to their usual height.

Scott Kelly was reported to be about 2 inches taller after nearly a year on the International Space Station. That figure is a reported, approximate case, not a result guaranteed on every mission.

Simplified illustrations: the astronaut is a drawing, not a portrait, and the height difference and spine are shown schematically.
